title: Give future 0.3 source builds an explicit development identity

requirement.summary: Prevent a wheel built from future-0.3 development source from reporting the published stable 0.2.1 identity before release review and publication.

objective.rationale: The independent installed-build pilot proved the source wheel and stable release could share the same displayed version even though their contents differed, which blocks trustworthy workflow pinning and release-candidate review.

goal: Set one PEP 440 future-0.3 development version across runtime and bundled compatibility metadata while retaining published stable and managed-consumer identities as historical external facts.
non_goals: Do not publish a wheel, tag, release, manifest asset, or package index entry.
Do not change the version or digest pinned by an existing stable consumer workflow.
Do not wire the Development Monitor into GitHub Actions or migrate NYC in this slice.
Do not claim release-candidate or stable readiness from a development identity.
acceptance_signals: Runtime and package metadata report 0.3.0.dev0 from the existing single version source.
Bundled current metadata declares the matching development channel and validates without claiming a published artifact digest.
Compatibility metadata includes published stable 0.2.1 as an eligible prior version without changing repository layout or migration claims.
Published stable 0.2.1 documentation and managed-consumer pins remain unchanged historical facts.
Focused package, release-metadata, and update tests pass, followed by the complete suite and repository governance check.

items: Update comparison could accidentally treat a published stable version as newer than the development runtime.
Bundled compatibility metadata could drift from the runtime version or make an unsupported migration claim.
Consumer workflow pins could be changed before a reviewed 0.3 artifact and digest exist.

stop_conditions: Stop if establishing a development identity requires changing a published tag, release asset, or consumer workflow.
Stop if runtime and bundled metadata cannot retain one version source without weakening manifest validation.
Stop if the change would imply release-candidate or stable approval.

decision.rationale: The user asked to continue today's work, and the completed installed pilot recorded this identity separation as a release blocker.
